Sam writes a list of natural numbers. The list has three perfect cubes and three perfect squares. If no number in the list has more than two digits, what is the MINIMUM number of distinct numbers he must have written?
a) 3
b) 4
c) 5
d) 6
My answer
Dyna Thinking Coach
Vault
pick what you already know
List what you know: the squares up to 99, and the cubes up to 99.
Echo
say it in your own words
Say it in your own words: "Which numbers can count as a square and a cube at the same time?"
YOUR TURN
Use those numbers first. How many more do you need?

If AB is a two-digit number whose cube is in the form of a 4-digit number “_ _ _ C” such that A < C < B, how many different values can C have?
a) 2
b) 3
c) 4
d) More than 4
My answer
Dyna Thinking Coach
Starter
decide how to begin
Begin with the size: which two-digit numbers have a 4-digit cube? Try 103 and 223.
Roots
ask why it works
Ask why only the last digit matters: the last digit of a cube comes from the last digit of the number. When is it smaller?
YOUR TURN
Check each possible AB against A < C < B.

56 × k is a perfect cube where k is a natural number. What could be the smallest possible value of k?
a) 36
b) 49
c) 56
d) 72
My answer
Dyna Thinking Coach
Slicer
break it into small parts
Break 56 into prime factors: 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7.
Vault
pick what you already know
Remember: in a perfect cube every prime factor comes in groups of three. Which group is not complete?
YOUR TURN
Multiply the missing factors to get k.
